title: Unordered pointed isomorphisms and their universal parameter
statement: For a morphism $f:W\to S$ with $n\geq0$ sections $s_i:S\to W$ satisfying $f\circ s_i=\mathrm{id}_S$, define its underlying pair to have curve $W\to S$, marking scheme $D=\coprod_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)}S$ with structural map $\coprod_i\mathrm{id}_S$, and inclusion $\coprod_i s_i:D\to W$. This is a canonical instance of the raw pair of [def-trf-semistable-multipointed-pair], without imposing a stability predicate. Let $P=(X,D,i)$ and $Q=(X',D',i')$ be pairs over a scheme $S$ [def-trf-semistable-multipointed-pair]. An unordered pointed isomorphism is an isomorphism of the marking arrows in the arrow category of schemes over $S$: two isomorphisms $a:D\simeq D'$ and $b:X\simeq X'$ over $S$ with $i'\circ a=b\circ i$. When $i,i'$ are closed immersions, $a$ is uniquely determined by $b$, and these are exactly the curve isomorphisms carrying the marked union onto the marked union as closed subschemes. Canonical base change uses the recorded pullback functor on pairs and its induced functor on arrows [def-pc-fibre-product]. For a morphism $c:T\to I$ of $S$-schemes and an $S$-scheme $Y$, the parameter map $Y_T\to Y_I$ is the fibre-product map induced by $\mathrm{id}_Y,c,\mathrm{id}_S$. An unordered pointed isomorphism $e:P_I\simeq Q_I$ over an $S$-scheme $I$ is universal if for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every unordered pointed isomorphism $e_T:P_T\simeq Q_T$, there is exactly one $c:T\to I$ over $S$ for which $e_T=c^*e$. Equivalently, both its curve and marking morphisms, composed with the canonical projections to $X'$ and $D'$, equal the corresponding parameter map followed by $e$ and the projection. This universal property is representability of the unordered pointed isomorphism functor, with its specified universal element. It includes arbitrary disconnected and nonreduced test schemes.
